Please answer this question with a number--which of the following best apply to the design in the study: 
        (1) totally fun first (i.e., Entertainment game reappropriated), 
        (2) mostly fun first (i.e., design workshop with disabled stakeholders),
        (3) both fun and utility first (i.e., design workshop with diverse stakeholders), 
        (4) mostly utility first (i.e., primary utilitarian mechanic designed first),
        (5) totally utility first (i.e., made by clinicians or specialists, fun incorporated later)
reasoning: The study is a set of design workshops with diverse stakeholder groups (librarians, engineers, interaction designers, TVIs/O&M specialists, volunteers) collaboratively creating purposeful assistive tactile graphics for children with visual impairments. The focus is on educational/assistive utility (learning goals, guidelines, child’s learning context) while also involving varied, non-clinician stakeholders and amateur-friendly tools, indicating a co-design process balancing utility and broader stakeholder perspectives rather than purely clinical or purely entertainment aims. This best matches a design that is both fun and utility first with diverse stakeholders.

Please answer this question with a number--which of the following best apply to the design in the study: 
        (1) unstructured play (i.e., no rules, making art),
        (2) semi-structured play (i.e., playground activities),
        (3) flexible structure with rules (i.e., improv),
        (4) flexible game (i.e., board game with house rules),
        (5) game with rigid rules (i.e., video game)
reasoning: Participants engaged in a structured design task with clear goals and constraints (designing 3D-printed tactile picture books using guidelines, specific tools, and templates), but within that they collaboratively made many design decisions (choice of book, page division, layout, modeling approaches). This is not free/unstructured play, nor a rigid rules game; it is a flexible, rule-guided creative activity, best matching flexible structure with rules (3).

Please answer this question with a number--which of the following best apply to the design in the study: 
        (1) entirely skill-based (i.e., trivia, sports),
        (2) mostly skill-based (i.e., mario kart),
        (3) equally skill and chance-based (i.e., catan),
        (4) mostly chance-based (i.e., Uno),
        (5) entirely chance-based (i.e., all dice)
reasoning: The study is a series of design workshops where participants create 3D-printed adaptive tactile picture books. Outcomes depend on participants’ knowledge and abilities in five identified skillsets (development, literacy, tactile graphicacy, task management, modeling), and participants actively apply and develop these skills during the task. There is no randomization or chance mechanism affecting success; performance is determined by participants’ skills and design decisions, making the task entirely skill-based.

        (4) mostly social, but aspects are independent (i.e., house on hill haunt transition),

reasoning: The study is based on group design workshops and a proposed collaborative online platform. Participants work together in domain-based groups (librarians, engineers, interaction designers, TVIs, volunteers) on shared 3DP-ATP design tasks, dividing pages, defining templates, and coordinating roles. The future tool is explicitly framed around team-building, communication, and collaborative project work. The design activity is therefore entirely social rather than solo.

Please answer this question with a number--which of the following best apply to the design in the study: 
        (1) entirely turn-based (i.e., tic tac toe),
        (2) follows a set of steps (i.e., viticulture's dynamic turn ordering),
        (3) turns are taken, but some actions can be taken at any time (i.e., pandemic),
        (4) most actions can be taken at any time, but there are some phases (i.e., PvP death reset timer),
        (5) entirely simultaneous (i.e., race)
reasoning: The study is about a collaborative design process for 3D-printed tactile picture books, structured into activities/roles (need assessment, content selection, modeling, etc.), which implies a workflow that follows a set of steps rather than discrete turns or fully simultaneous action. There is no indication of turn-taking mechanics or real-time simultaneous interaction, so the best fit is a stepwise process (2).

Please answer this question with a number--which of the following best apply to the design in the study: 
        (1) entirely synchronous (i.e., real time strategy game),
        (2) mostly synchronous with a few asynchronous affordances (i.e., league of legends),
        (3) equal mix of synchronous and asynchronous affordances (i.e., helldivers 2),
        (4) mostly asynchronous with few synchronous affordances (i.e. cookie clicker),
        (5) entirely asynchronous (i.e., chess by postage mail)
reasoning: The work is about collaborative design of 3D-printed tactile picture books via workshops and a proposed online collaborative platform. Collaboration centers on tasks like proposing projects, allocating work, and contributing designs, which are naturally done at different times. The paper explicitly discusses supporting both synchronous and asynchronous collaboration, but the core activities (designing, modeling, printing, commenting) are not real-time interactive in the sense of a game; they are predominantly asynchronous with some synchronous coordination (e.g., workshops, possible real-time communication features). This best matches a mostly asynchronous design with a few synchronous affordances.

Please answer this question with a number--which of the following best apply to the design in the study: 
        (1) entirely symmetrical (i.e., tic tac toe),
        (2) mostly symmetrical (i.e., undertale's differing NPC behaviors based on previous playthroughs),
        (3) both symmetrical and asymmetrical (i.e., pandemic with its similar turn structure but different character abilities),
        (4) mostly asymmetrical (i.e., tag),
        (5) entirely asymmetrical (i.e., keep talking, nobody explodes)
reasoning: All workshop participants engage in the same overarching design task with similar workshop structure and tools (symmetrical structure), but they have systematically different roles, expertise, and dominant skillsets (End-User Advocate, Content Translator, Task Manager, Modeler), making their functional contributions asymmetric. This combination of shared task framework plus differentiated abilities and roles best matches a design that is both symmetrical and asymmetrical.
